newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST - Anglo interim share seen richer.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Anglo interim share seen richer.

text.p: Robust earnings from its coal operations and satisfactory results from other divisions are likely to drive Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd's half year earnings higher, analysts said on Wednesday.
But they added the richer profits forecast for the six months ended September were not helped by the group's gold operations which posted fairly flat interim results last month.
Anglo is due to announce interim results on Tuesday.
Analysts polled by Reuters ranged Anglo's total interim earnings per share between 1,035.0 cents and 1,130.0 cents with consensus at 1,070 cents and compared to 837 cents previously.
They said that a dividend would likely stand between 150.0 cents per share and 160.0 cents with consensus at 153.0 cents, compared to 130 cents per share previously.
"The rise in earnings is basically due to strength across the board. It is mostly carried by the coal side but industrials also helped," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.
Anglo American Coal Corp Ltd raised its earnings for the six months ended September to 1,680.4 cents per share from 1,283.6 cents per share previously.

Amcoal said then that the surge in its profit was largely due to the rand's dramatic shedding of more than 30 percent of its value against the dollar since February. This had boosted export prices and would continue to do so in the second half.
Amcoal declared a 420.0 cents dividend, from 300 cents.

Despite a slip in attributable earnings at Anglo American Industrial Corp Ltd to 427 million rand from 471 million rand, analysts said the operation had performed satisfactorily and would underpin the boost given by Amcoal.
Amic said the softer earnings for its first half ended June was on account of weak commodity markets and it forecast a rise in second half earnings, boosted by the weaker rand.
Analysts said Anglo American Gold Corp Ltd had disappointed over the last six months to June and would contribute little to the group's better first half earnings.
The weaker rand should have enriched Amgold's earnings by a greater extent but didn't, analysts said. Net earnings fell to 229 million rand from 264 million rand previously.
"The gold division (profit) should have been up, maybe by as much as 70 percent. But Amgold wasn't. It was basically flat, if not worse," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.
